references.text: Caleb, son of Jephunneh, is mentioned as the spy from the tribe of Judah who was sent out to explore the land of Canaan.
Joshua, son of Nun, is mentioned as the spy from the tribe of Ephraim.
God promises that Caleb will be allowed to enter the land because he had a different spirit and followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
Only Caleb and Joshua from the entire generation were allowed to enter the promised land.
Joshua and Caleb were the only spies who survived because they remained faithful.
Confirmation that only Caleb and Joshua survived among those mustered in the wilderness of Sinai.
Moses recounts that Caleb would be allowed to see the land because he followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
Caleb reminds Joshua of the promise given by Moses because he followed the Lord, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly.
Hebron was given to Caleb the Kenizzite because he followed the Lord, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly.
Caleb, son of Jephunneh, received his inheritance in Hebron as commanded.
Othniel, son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, is mentioned and confirms Caleb's Kenizzite lineage.
